sentence: Igår läste studenten som hade kommit från Uppsala den bok som professorn hade rekommenderat.

derivationStages.statement: Establish the base structure, argument positions, and the two restrictive relative clauses.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The sentence is built with NP-based X-bar projections. Studenten and professorn are inflected definite nouns; den occupies the determiner position of the object NP. Each restrictive relative CP adjoins to the nominal N′ it modifies. Som is a complementizer, not an argument: a silent relative operator initially occupies the subject position of hade kommit and the object position of hade rekommenderat. Läste assigns Agent to studenten and Theme to the book NP. Kommit assigns Theme to its subject operator and Source to från Uppsala. Rekommenderat assigns Agent to professorn and Theme to its object operator. Från assigns its locative role to Uppsala. The embedded finite auxiliaries assign nominative to their subjects; från assigns oblique Case to Uppsala, and the transitive verbs assign accusative to their objects. Each occurrence of hade selects a VP with a supine lexical verb, giving the relative clause its pluperfect interpretation. Igår is initially a right-adjoined VP modifier and locates the reading event yesterday. The main finite inflection and the matrix complementizer are initially silent; subsequent stages establish the matrix verb's head-movement chain.

derivationStages.statement: Form the subject-relative and object-relative operator chains.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First, the silent subject operator moves from the subject position of hade kommit to the specifier of its relative CP, leaving a nominative subject trace. The operator locally A′-binds that trace; Swedish relative som licenses this subject-relative configuration, so an English-style that-trace prohibition is not imposed. The resulting CP restricts studenten through the correspondence between its nominal head and the operator variable. Next, the silent object operator moves from the complement of rekommenderat to the specifier of the second relative CP, leaving an accusative object trace. This operator locally A′-binds its trace, which remains properly governed by rekommenderat. That CP restricts bok through the corresponding nominal-head/operator dependency. Both movements remain within their respective relative clauses; neither crosses the other relative clause. Hade stays in I in each relative, and som stays in C.

derivationStages.statement: Move the matrix lexical verb to finite I.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Läste moves from the matrix V position and adjoins to the immediately higher finite I, leaving a silent verbal trace. The pronounced verb retains its lexical occurrence at the landing site, while the complex I head combines it with the silent past inflection. This is the first step of successive head movement rather than a direct jump from V to C. The resulting finite I governs the matrix subject studenten and assigns it nominative Case. The book NP retains accusative through the lexical verb's chain, and the subject remains in Spec-IP.

derivationStages.statement: Move the matrix finite verb from I to C.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex finite I containing läste moves from its established position above VP and adjoins to the matrix declarative C. A silent I trace remains above VP, completing the successive V-to-I-to-C head-movement chain. The matrix subject stays in Spec-IP and therefore follows the verb in C. The embedded auxiliaries do not undergo this operation: their relative complementizer positions are already occupied by som. Matrix nominative licensing is preserved through the finite-head chain.

values.result: matrix finite verb precedes the subject

derivationStages.statement: Front Igår and complete the Swedish V2 structure and binding analysis.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Igår moves from its established VP-adjoined position to matrix Spec-CP, leaving a silent adverbial trace. The fronted phrase A′-binds that trace and is interpreted as the temporal modifier of the reading event, not of either embedded event. With Igår in Spec-CP and läste in C, the matrix clause satisfies Swedish V2: one constituent precedes the finite verb, and studenten remains immediately after it in Spec-IP. The relative clauses retain som in C and hade in I. The referential NPs studenten, den bok som professorn hade rekommenderat, professorn, and Uppsala have no coindexed c-commanding antecedents and satisfy Binding Principle C. The relative operators bind variables through A′-chains rather than functioning as personal pronouns or reflexive anaphors; consequently, no additional Principle A or Principle B dependency is required. The pronounced terminals now give the input sentence in its exact word order.
